bugs: Admin endpoint can't be reached in production. routes/api.php:7-8 protects it with the default `auth` (session `web` guard), but the stateless `api` group has no StartSession and there's no token guard (no Sanctum). Only `actingAs` in tests can authenticate.

Raw event isn't stored in full. PaymentWebhookController.php:16 saves `$request->validated()` as the payload, so any keys in `data` beyond payment_id/refund_id/amount are silently dropped. A probe with data.extra lost it.

Signed but schema-invalid events (for example an unknown shape, or refund.created without refund_id) get a 422 and are never stored. Each such delivery should be recorded once and fail visibly instead of bouncing.
A missing Order (`firstOrFail`, ProcessWebhookEvent.php:62) is a permanent condition, but it is retried up to MaxExceptions(5) with backoff before it fails.
antipatterns: app/Notifications/PaymentReceipt.php:10: the receipt notification is not ShouldQueue, so mail is sent synchronously inside the worker job and an SMTP failure triggers a whole job retry.
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:68-76: order updates and event status changes are not wrapped in a transaction, so a partial failure leaves the order updated while the event is still `processing`.
routes/api.php:8: `can:viewAny,'.WebhookEvent::class` string middleware; `->can('viewAny', WebhookEvent::class)` reads more cleanly.
app/Http/Middleware/VerifyPaymentSignature.php:18: strtolower on the incoming signature is harmless, but it is unrequested leniency.
strengths: Clean job: WithoutOverlapping keyed on event_id, RateLimited('payments-api') with Limit::perSecond(10), Backoff/MaxExceptions/Timeout/DeleteWhenMissingModels/WithoutRelations attributes, retryUntil, failed() marks the event failed with the error.
429 is handled by release with Retry-After, 4xx by fail(), and 5xx are rethrown so they retry with backoff.
Order transitions use conditional UPDATE...WHERE status IN (atomic, no downgrade), and the receipt_sent_at guard prevents duplicate receipts.
createOrFirst plus wasRecentlyCreated gives race-safe idempotent ingestion.
MassPrunable with model:prune scheduled daily, onOneServer and withoutOverlapping.

Excellent tests: real database queue driven by queue:work --once with time travel. They prove the 5xx is released with a delay and then succeeds, that exhausted retries mark the event failed and land in failed_jobs, and they cover rate-limit release and lock release, plus datasets for validation.
README worker section is accurate (numprocs, process_name, timeouts, queue:restart, shared cache).

bugs: refund.created without refund_id/amount isn't validated anywhere. ProcessWebhookEvent::refundCreated casts to (string)/(int) and creates a Refund with provider_refund_id '' and amount 0. A second, different refund event with no ID is then silently deduped by createOrFirst and still marked processed (confirmed by probe).

PaymentProvider::payment() (app/Services/PaymentProvider.php:17-25) declares an `array` return type, but a 200 with an empty or non-JSON body returns null and throws a TypeError, which is retried before it fails.

README Supervisor snippet uses `numprocesses` (should be `numprocs`) and leaves out process_name, so numprocs>1 wouldn't work. It also says retry_after(90) < stopwaitsecs, yet the snippet sets stopwaitsecs=60.
antipatterns: app/Console/Commands/RedispatchStuckWebhookEvents.php plus the five-minute schedule: extra ceremony the task didn't ask for. It can enqueue duplicate jobs for events that are just waiting in a deep backlog; isFinished and the lock make that safe, but it adds moving parts.
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:98-100: throws a RuntimeException when the provider status isn't 'succeeded', turning a business mismatch into an exception-driven retry and fail loop.
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:37-41: docblock comment narrating middleware ordering rationale.
Dedicated `webhooks` queue set via onQueue in the constructor. It's fine, but workers must be configured or jobs never run; the README does document it.
strengths: Queued receipt notification with ShouldQueue + ShouldQueueAfterCommit, sent from inside a DB::transaction, so mail only goes out after the order commit.

Same solid job design: WithoutOverlapping plus RateLimited middleware, Backoff/MaxExceptions/Timeout/DeleteWhenMissingModels attributes, retryUntil, 429 release / 4xx fail / 5xx rethrow, failed() marks the event failed.
markFailed is a conditional update that never overwrites a Processed event, and transitions return a bool so only the winning transition notifies.
Sanctum installed and `auth:sanctum` with ->can() on the admin route, so the endpoint is actually usable by API clients; redirectGuestsTo returns 401 JSON for the API.
Stores every signed event, including unknown types or a missing payment_id, and fails them visibly, which matches 'store every event'.

Tests use withFakeQueueInteractions()->assertReleased(delay: 7) / assertFailed(), Sanctum::actingAs, Queue::assertPushedOn, and lock/limiter blocking via dispatchSync. Broad failure-path coverage, though there's no real-queue backoff/exhaustion run like impl-1's.

v.rationale: The two are very close: same architecture, middleware stack, attribute-based retry config and atomic order transitions. impl-2 wins on the queue focus area and on real usability. Its receipt notification is queued and commits only after the transaction (ShouldQueueAfterCommit inside DB::transaction), whereas impl-1 sends mail synchronously in the worker with no transaction. impl-2's admin endpoint uses Sanctum and works for real API clients. impl-1's uses session `auth` on the stateless api group, so in production only tests can reach it. impl-1 also silently drops unvalidated keys from the stored payload and 422s signed events instead of storing them. impl-2 has its own real bug: refund.created with no refund_id creates an empty-ID, zero-amount refund and dedups later ones. It also throws a TypeError on an empty provider body, has a README Supervisor typo, and adds an over-engineered stuck-event redispatcher. impl-1's tests are the stronger suite (real database-queue runs that prove backoff and exhaustion), which narrows the gap but doesn't close it. Every probe file was deleted after running.
